en.location: 📍 Losser/Oldenzaal, Losser municipality · Estate · Medium-sized
en.description: The De Snippert estate reaches back to the nineteenth century, when wealthy families used it as hunting ground and country retreat; the stately houses and farms still testify to that prosperous time. Today it belongs to Natuurmonumenten and alternates wood, heath and avenues, with purple-flowering heath in August and blooming rhododendrons in spring. In autumn you can gather sweet chestnuts, and in the wood live green woodpecker, jay, nuthatch and wren. A 3.8 km walk starts at the Judithhoeve.

In de jaren dertig kocht de Enschedese textielfamilie Blijdenstein het als productiebos: bomen in keurige rijen voor het hout. Sinds 1969 is het van Natuurmonumenten en krijgt de natuur weer ruimte: dood hout blijft liggen, en soorten keren terug — sperwer, bosuil, ransuil, grauwe klauwier en geelgors. tags: Wood · from production forest to natural wood
en.location: 📍 Losser/Oldenzaal, Losser municipality · Nature area · Medium-sized
en.description: The Haagse Bos near Losser has nothing to do with The Hague: the name comes from Haagerbrook, “Haegenbroeick” — a wet, low-lying piece of land in the old marke. In the 1930s the Enschede textile family Blijdenstein bought it as a production forest: trees in neat rows for timber. Since 1969 it has belonged to Natuurmonumenten and nature gets room again: dead wood stays put and species return — sparrowhawk, tawny owl, long-eared owl, red-backed shrike and yellowhammer. In spring may lily and periwinkle flower, in autumn the fly agaric.

nl.location: 📍 Lonneker, gemeente Enschede · Natuurgebied · Middelgroot
nl.description: De Lonnekerberg is met zijn zestig meter het hoogste punt in de wijde omgeving van Enschede en vormt de zuidelijkste uitloper van het stuwwalcomplex Oldenzaal–Enschede, zo’n 140.000 jaar geleden door landijs opgestuwd. Het was ooit een houtproductiebos met vooral naaldhout, maar sinds het jaar 2000 beheert Landschap Overijssel het gebied en keert het natuurlijke karakter terug: loofbos, heldere bronnen en bijzondere soorten als breedbladige wespenorchis, stijve ogentroost en duizendguldenkruid. De Jufferbeek kronkelt erdoorheen, en in de oude kleigaten — resten van een steenfabriek — liggen stille vijvers. Langs het bessenpad groeien framboos, braam en bosbes, en diep in het beukenbos ligt het graf van textielfabrikant Blijdenstein.

tags: Ridge woodland · hill wood with springs and clay pits
en.location: 📍 Lonneker, Enschede municipality · Nature area · Medium-sized
en.description: The Lonnekerberg is, at sixty metres, the highest point in the wide surroundings of Enschede and forms the southernmost outlier of the Oldenzaal–Enschede ice-pushed ridge, pushed up by land ice some 140,000 years ago. It was once a timber-production forest of mainly conifers, but since the year 2000 Landschap Overijssel manages the area and its natural character is returning: broad-leaved woodland, clear springs and special species such as broad-leaved helleborine, stiff eyebright and common centaury. The Jufferbeek winds through it, and the old clay pits — remnants of a brickyard — hold quiet ponds. Along the berry path grow raspberry, bramble and bilberry, and deep in the beech wood lies the grave of textile manufacturer Blijdenstein.

nl.description: Het Weusthagpark is het groene hart van Hengelo: een park van zo’n 200 hectare dat in ruim honderd jaar organisch is gegroeid en niet is aangelegd. Het begon met de kleigaten van de steenbakkerij van de familie Rientjes en het oude landgoed De Houtmaat, waar begin twintigste eeuw nog een sanatorium voor tuberculosepatiënten stond. De natuurlijke kernen zijn het Van Alphenbos en de Plassen van Rientjes, en sinds de wederopbouw groeide het uit tot een volwaardig stadspark met heemtuin, beleefbos, biologische moestuin en kinderboerderij. Omdat Vitens er drinkwater wint, blijft het park gevrijwaard van bebouwing — en ontving het de Green Flag Award voor de kwaliteit van het openbaar groen.

tags: City park · woodland, water and heemtuin in Hengelo
en.location: 📍 Hengelo, Hengelo municipality · City park · c. 200 ha
en.description: The Weusthagpark is the green heart of Hengelo: a park of about 200 hectares that grew organically over more than a hundred years rather than being laid out. It began with the clay pits of the Rientjes family brickyard and the old De Houtmaat estate, which early in the twentieth century still housed a sanatorium for tuberculosis patients. Its natural cores are the Van Alphenbos and the Plassen van Rientjes, and since the post-war reconstruction it has grown into a full city park with a heemtuin, a play-and-discover wood, an organic vegetable garden and a petting farm. Because Vitens extracts drinking water here, the park remains free of development — and it has received the Green Flag Award for the quality of its public green space.

en.location: 📍 Enschede/Hengelo, Enschede municipality · Estate · c. 114 ha
en.description: The De Wildernis estate lies between Hengelo and Enschede and belongs, like the neighbouring Lonnekermeer and Haverriet, to the Landgoederen van Textiel — once owned by Twente textile manufacturers. It is a varied estate of woods, heathland and old farmland, through which several brooks flow down from the Lonnekerberg, such as the Elsbeek, Eschbeek and Vanekerbeek. In the northern Hartjesbos lie heathland and hay meadows ringed by hedge banks that were once irrigated with brook water — an old form of fertilising. To the south the Sterrenbos joins it with its monumental avenue pattern. The part along the Hofmeijerweg is freely accessible; the rest is a quiet zone.

tags: Estate · 800 years of history on the north edge of Enschede
en.location: 📍 Enschede, Enschede municipality · Estate · Medium-sized
en.description: The Hof Espelo estate on the north edge of Enschede is one of the oldest Twente estates: as early as 28 May 1215 Pope Innocent III confirmed that the Chapter of St Peter in Utrecht was its owner. More than eight centuries of history have since left their mark here. In the eighteenth century the tenant Gabriël Davina became owner after a long legal battle, and to this day heath, fields, woodland and brooks alternate around the villa, the coach house (now a visitor centre) and old Twente farmhouses. Special details are the old fish pond and the aircraft mounds (splitter boxes) from the Second World War, in which aircraft were hidden. Landschap Overijssel manages the estate.

tags: Estate · country seat with heath and the Zwarte Ven in Twekkelo
en.location: 📍 Twekkelo, Enschede municipality · Estate · c. 70 ha
en.description: The Het Stroot estate lies in the hamlet of Twekkelo, between Enschede and Hengelo. It was founded in 1819 by Johanna Berendina Roessingh-van Heek, who had a small country house built beside the old farm; in 1865 the textile magnate Gerrit Jan van Heek bought the property and had the garden architect Dirk Wattez lay out a landscape park around 1876. The villa (1840) with its coach house, farmhouse and a seventeenth-century sandstone entrance gate together form a national monument. Its natural heart is the Zwarte Ven, a pool of exceptional clarity with marsh pennywort, dwarf spike-rush and water purslane, ringed by the largest heathland of Twekkelo. The pool itself is not accessible; the paths around it are.

tags: Estate · park woodland and mansion between Enschede and Losser
en.location: 📍 Enschede, Enschede municipality · Estate · c. 14 ha
en.description: The De Hooge Boekel estate lies between Enschede and Losser and counts among the most distinctive estates of Enschede. Around 1900 it consisted of farmhouses, farmland and production woodland, which the Van Heek textile family bought in the mid-nineteenth century as hunting ground. Herman van Heek had a garden designed by the Delden landscape architect Pieter Wattez, and in 1926 the mansion was completed. Its centrepiece is a T-shaped pond — swimming and rowing pond in one — fringed by conical trees. After years of decline (the estate was even briefly owned by followers of the Maharishi), the entrepreneur Herman Kok restored the overgrown sightlines and the pond. The surrounding Hoge Boekel is a typical Twente hedgerow landscape, ’the garden of the city’.

en.description: The Galgenven is a hidden, small-scale fen in the borderland between Losser and Enschede. It is not accessible, and precisely for that reason it is a quiet place for the great crested newt, which can breed in the shallow, fish-free water. On the damp edges grow special species such as the marsh gentian and the delicate common dodder, a parasitic bindweed that twines around heather shrubs. The fen is managed by Natuurmonumenten and is best viewed from the Oude Losserseweg, from where you look out over the small-scale hedgerow landscape.

tags: Wood · mixed woodland on the tip of the Oldenzaalseveen
en.location: 📍 Losser/Enschede, Losser municipality · Woodland · Small
en.description: De Tip is a narrow, wooded nature area on the Lossersestraat between Losser and Enschede — the name comes from its position on the extreme point (tip) of the former Oldenzaalseveen estate, which lies across the road. Together with the Haagse Bos it forms an ecological corridor on the east side of Enschede. Originally it consisted of heath and conifer woodland; Natuurmonumenten is converting it to mixed broad-leaved woodland with wet heath patches, so young birch, beech and oak are appearing. The wood is remarkably rich in fungi such as fly agaric and honey fungus, and with luck you may see a roe deer or pine marten.

en.description: Penninkskotten is an old kamp — a small-scale reclamation island in the wild grounds — between Losser and Enschede, near the Haagse Bos. Together with the Broekheurner Heege and De Zweede near Boekelo it belongs to the characteristic kamps of the Twente countryside, where hedge banks and tree rows around the arable fields kept out livestock and wind. On the Penninkskottenweg stands an old glacial boulder that marked the boundary between the Losser and Lonneker markes. The black sand betrays the former peat, and at Whitsun the Pinksterfeesten with car rodeo and tractor pulling bring the place alive. A name- and landscape-entry in the heart of the Twente hedgerow landscape.

en.location: 📍 Losser/Enschede, Losser municipality · Nature area · Small
en.description: Lindermaten is a varied nature area between Losser and Enschede, managed by Natuurmonumenten: wet woods, damp grasslands and scattered wild-flower plots, where poppy, oxeye daisy and cornflower attract insects. On the south side flows the Elsbeek, which was given more room and now meanders more freely through the landscape; at high water part of the woodland and grasslands floods. In spring the oxlip flowers here, one of the first spring blooms, preferably in the company of white wood anemones. A special piece of heritage is the medieval landweer — an earthen rampart that formed part of the defence lines around De Lutte, Losser and Oldenzaal — which is being made visible again.

en.description: De Krabbe is an old farmstead near the Twente village of Beuningen, between Denekamp and Losser. In the Oldenzaal district, to which Beuningen belonged, no farm of that name was recorded in 1601 — the countryside lay ’wild’ and deserted because of the Eighty Years’ War — but in the eighteenth century the Krabbe family farmed there for generations, including the farmer Lambert Jan Krabbe. Later the holding passed to the Groeneveld family, who lived there until the late twentieth century. The last owner sold the farmhouse on the Paandersdijk to the Twente comedian Herman Finkers, who dismantled it and had a new house built a little further on from the old materials. A name-entry that preserves the farming history of Twente.

nl.description: De Pan van Persijn — kortweg het Panbos — is een bosrijk stuk binnenduinrand van Berkheide bij Katwijk. De naam herinnert aan de Heren van Persijn, een oud adellijk geslacht met een kasteel in Wassenaar, dat hier een jachtgebied had; de ’pan’ is een uitgeblazen vochtige duinvallei. Vanaf het begin van de twintigste eeuw was het landgoed in gebruik als weide- en teelgrond, en in de Tweede Wereldoorlog werd het onderdeel van de Atlantikwall — de anderhalve meter dikke muur met drakentanden in de zuidwesthoek is er nog te zien. Nu liggen er een hertenkamp, eenden- en ganzenvijvers, speelweiden en een theehuis, als onderdeel van Nationaal Park Hollandse Duinen.

en.description: The Pan van Persijn — simply the Panbos — is a wooded piece of the inner-dune edge of Berkheide near Katwijk. The name recalls the Heren van Persijn, an old noble family with a castle in Wassenaar that held a hunting ground here; the ’pan’ is a blown-out damp dune valley. From the early twentieth century the estate was used as grazing and arable land, and in the Second World War it became part of the Atlantikwall — the one-and-a-half-metre-thick wall with dragon’s teeth in its south-west corner can still be seen. The municipality of Katwijk bought the wood in 1955 from the Jochems family. Today it holds a deer park, duck and goose ponds, play meadows and a tea house, as part of Nationaal Park Hollandse Duinen.

nl.description: De Leidse Hout is het volkspark van Leiden, een bospark van zo’n twintig hectare op de grens van Leiden en Oegstgeest. Het idee kwam in 1919 van raadslid Johannes Knuttel: een park voor alle lagen van de Leidse bevolking. Met een schenking van fabrikant Johan de Koster (meelfabriek De Sleutels) en het ontwerp van landschapsarchitect Klaas van Nes ging in 1928 de aanleg van start — werklozen groeven het drassige veen af en hieven het terrein op. Op 30 juni 1931 opende het park, met een grote vijver, een hertenkamp (1935) en later het theehuis. In de oorlog verdwenen zo’n 2000 bomen in de kachels; het park herrees na de bevrijding, met muziektent, openluchttheater en een altijd bewoond ooievaarsnest.

en.location: 📍 Leiden/Oegstgeest, Leiden municipality · City park · c. 20 ha
en.description: The Leidse Hout is the people’s park of Leiden, a woodland park of about twenty hectares on the border of Leiden and Oegstgeest. The idea came in 1919 from councillor Johannes Knuttel: a park for all layers of Leiden’s population. With a donation from the factory owner Johan de Koster (the De Sleutels flour mill) and a design by the landscape architect Klaas van Nes, work began in 1928 — the unemployed dug away the soggy peat and raised the ground. On 30 June 1931 the park opened, with a large pond, a deer park (1935) and later the tea house. During the war some 2,000 trees ended up in people’s stoves; the park rose again after the liberation, with a bandstand, an open-air theatre and an ever-occupied stork’s nest.

en.description: The Oud Poelgeest country seat in Oegstgeest goes back to a medieval castle, destroyed by Spanish troops in 1573 during the siege of Leiden. On its foundations a new, symmetrical house in classicist Italian style rose in 1668. Between 1724 and 1738 it was the summer residence of Herman Boerhaave, the famous Leiden professor of medicine and botany, who grew exotic trees and rare plants here. In the nineteenth century the house gained two octagonal towers with pear-shaped spires, giving it its castle-like appearance. Today it is a congress hotel, surrounded by ten hectares of park woodland with abundant spring flora and a Grand Canal running to the Haarlemmertrekvaart.

Its south side is a wooded quiet zone, separated by a fence, with walking, running and cycling paths; on the Joppe side lie a brasserie, a large playground and allotments. tags: Country seat · seventeenth-century ensemble with ten national monuments
en.location: 📍 Warmond, Teylingen municipality · Country seat · c. 11 ha
en.description: The Oostergeest country seat lies just outside the village centre of Warmond and is a remarkably well-preserved historical ensemble with elements from five successive centuries — no fewer than ten national monuments on almost eleven hectares. Its history begins in 1651, when Cornelis van Rosenburgh, schout of Warmond, bought a farm here and extended it into the manor ’De Hoop’. In 1726 it passed to the Rotterdam auctioneer Cornelis Schrijver, who rebuilt house and garden in the French garden fashion with a star wood and a menagerie, and gave it the name Oostergeest. Since 1850 six generations of the Leemans family lived on the estate; in 2023 they transferred it to the Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser. In the middle of the meadow the inhabited stork’s nest still stands.

tags: Estate · castle, fairytale wood and restored orangery
en.location: 📍 Warmond, Teylingen municipality · Estate · c. 23 ha
en.description: The Huys te Warmont estate in Warmond breathes grandeur: a castle-like house on foundations from the twelfth or thirteenth century, surrounded by a park-like fairytale wood of yews, swamp cypresses and old oak avenues. Its most famous resident was Johan van Duvenvoirde (1577–1645), admiral of Holland and commander among the Sea Beggars; after the destruction by the Spanish he was allowed to rebuild the house with stones from demolished Warmond monasteries. The Haarlem mayor Baron van Leijden gave the house its present appearance. The orangery and the garden by Springer and Tersteeg (around 1920) have been restored to their former glory, with Solomon’s seals and hart’s-tongue ferns in diamond patterns, and the castle moat vanishes into the wood as the Droomvijver. The Zuid-Hollands Landschap manages the estate.

De plassen dienen als boezemwater voor het Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland en zijn het oudste watersportgebied van Nederland, met tradities als de Kaagweek, de Turf- en Strontrace en de Schippertjesdagen. tags: Peat lakes · lake district between Leiden, Warmond and the Kaag
en.location: 📍 Warmond/Kaag, Teylingen municipality · Peat lakes · Large
en.description: The Kagerplassen between Leiden, Warmond and the Kaag form a puzzle of about ten shallow peat lakes, fringed by reed beds and cut through by narrow ditches and canals. They arose in the Middle Ages through turf extraction, on peat that was repeatedly eroded by north-westerly storms after the Rhine mouth at Katwijk silted up — a remnant of the old Haarlemmermeer, reclaimed in 1852. The lakes serve as boezem (storage) water for the Rijnland water board and are the oldest water-sports area in the Netherlands, with traditions such as the Kaagweek, the Turf- en Strontrace and the Schippertjesdagen. On the Kaageiland the Royal van Lent shipyard builds the world-famous superyachts.

nl.location: 📍 Rijpwetering, gemeente Kaag en Braassem · Poldermolen · Rijksmonument
nl.description: De Blauwe Molen in Rijpwetering is een achtkante, rietgedekte poldermolen waarvan het deel onder de kap opvallend felblauw is geschilderd. De molen is in 1904 gebouwd door molenmaker Vrijburg uit Oud Ade, met een achtkant uit 1772 van een afgebroken boezemmolen uit Hillegersberg (Rotterdam). Tot 1960 bemaalde hij de Blauwe polder — circa 250 hectare, 1,55 meter opvoerhoogte. De polder zelf werd op 7 april 1629 gesticht als Oud Aasepolder en dankt zijn latere naam aan de voorganger van de molen, een wipmolen met een blauw geschilderd bovenhuis. De molenaarsfamilie Kraan bemaalde de polder ruim tachtig jaar; de laatste, Gerrit Kraan, werd door zijn enorme lengte en kracht een legendarisch figuur. De molen raakte buiten bedrijf in verval, werd rond 1968–1971 gerestaureerd en kan na de afdamming van de Achtwatering alleen nog in circuit malen.

tags: Polder mill · octagonal mill with a unique overtoom
en.location: 📍 Rijpwetering, Kaag en Braassem municipality · Polder mill · National monument
en.description: The Blauwe Molen in Rijpwetering is an octagonal, thatched polder mill whose section under the cap is painted a strikingly bright blue. It was built in 1904 by the millwright Vrijburg from Oud Ade, using an octagonal body from 1772 taken from a demolished boezem mill in Hillegersberg (Rotterdam). Until 1960 it drained the Blauwe polder — about 250 hectares, with a lift of 1.55 metres. The polder itself was founded on 7 April 1629 as the Oud Aasepolder and owes its later name to the mill’s predecessor, a wipmolen with a blue-painted upper body. The Kraan miller family drained the polder for over eighty years; the last of them, Gerrit Kraan, became a legendary figure for his enormous height and strength. After falling into disrepair the mill was restored around 1968–1971 and, since the damming of the Achtwatering, can only pump in circuit.

Het meer is na de eerste ontginningen in omvang verdubbeld door oeverafslag en het toestromende water uit nieuwe polders in de omgeving. Het staat in open verbinding met de Wijde Aa (via het Paddegat), die weer uitkomt op de Kromme Does bij Hoogmade, en is net als de Kagerplassen een geliefd watersportgebied met jachthavens, zeil- en surfwater. en.description: The Braassemermeer between Woubrugge, Rijnsaterwoude, Roelofarendsveen and Leimuiden is one of the few natural lakes in the Dutch peat country. After the first reclamations the lake doubled in size through bank erosion and the inflow of water from new polders in the surroundings. It is in open connection with the Wijde Aa (via the Paddegat), which in turn joins the Kromme Does near Hoogmade, and like the Kagerplassen it is a beloved water-sports area with marinas and sailing and windsurfing water. Rijnsaterwoude grew in the Middle Ages as a peat-reclamation settlement along the lake. Nearby lies the Vierambachtspolder, which was drained in 1744 by eleven windmills.

tags: Veenweidepolder · als laatste polder van Zuid-Holland drooggemalen
nl.location: 📍 Zoeterwoude, tussen Zoeterwoude en Stompwijk · Veenweidepolder · ca. 140 ha
nl.description: De Geerpolder ligt verscholen achter boerderij De Vierhuizen, tussen Zoeterwoude en Stompwijk. Voor de Gouden Eeuw bestond het hier uit twee polders — de Geerpolder en de kleine Blankaartpolder — waar een dik pakket veen via veenstroompjes afwaterde op de Oude Rijn. In de zeventiende en achttiende eeuw werd het veen uitgeveend voor turf, waarna het land deels onder water kwam te staan. Omdat het hoogteverschil te groot was voor een molengang, kon de polder pas met de komst van het stoomgemaal worden drooggelegd — in 1865, als laatste polder van Zuid-Holland. Wat tevoorschijn kwam was natte, zure katteklei. In de jaren zeventig werden plannen voor een recreatieplas dankzij verzet van bewoners en de gemeente Zoeterwoude afgeblazen, zodat het open veenweidelandschap bewaard bleef.

tags: Peat meadow polder · the last polder of South Holland to be drained
en.location: 📍 Zoeterwoude, between Zoeterwoude and Stompwijk · Peat meadow polder · c. 140 ha
en.description: The Geerpolder lies tucked away behind the De Vierhuizen farm, between Zoeterwoude and Stompwijk. Before the Dutch Golden Age this was two polders — the Geerpolder and the small Blankaartpolder — where a thick layer of peat drained into the Oude Rijn through small streams. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the peat was dug out for turf, after which the land partly came under water. Because the height difference was too great for a mill chain, the polder could only be drained once the steam pumping station arrived — in 1865, as the last polder of South Holland. What emerged was wet, sour cat’s clay (katteklei). In the 1970s plans for a recreation lake were abandoned after resistance from residents and the municipality of Zoeterwoude, preserving the open peat meadow landscape.

nl.location: 📍 Wassenaar, gemeente Wassenaar · Buitenplaats · Parkbos
nl.description: Buitenplaats Rust en Vreugd ligt aan de Rijksstraatweg, de oude weg tussen Den Haag en Leiden, en gaat terug tot een boerderij uit 1693. Rond 1754 kocht de Haagse notaris Johannes Bourcourd de afgebrande boerderij; zijn zoon Gabriël herbouwde haar en doopte het buitenverblijf ’Rust en Vruegde’ — een naam die symbool stond voor het buitenleven. In 1848 liet Eduard van der Oudermeulen een nieuw neoclassicistisch landhuis met koetshuis bouwen, met slingerpaden in een parkbos van vroege landschapsstijl. Vanaf 1904 was het bezit van de Rotterdamse reder Philippus van Ommeren en zijn echtgenote Alida de Voogt, bekend om hun liefdadigheid. In de oorlog diende de buitenplaats als opslag en lanceerstation voor V-2’s en werd ze gebombardeerd. Het oude landhuis werd in 1987 gesloopt, maar het park is sinds 1961 onderdeel van de openbaar toegankelijke Wassenaarse Landgoederenzone.

tags: Country seat · park woodland in early landscape style
en.location: 📍 Wassenaar, Wassenaar municipality · Country seat · Park woodland
en.description: The Rust en Vreugd country seat lies on the Rijksstraatweg, the old road between The Hague and Leiden, and goes back to a farmhouse of 1693. Around 1754 the Hague notary Johannes Bourcourd bought the burnt-down farm; his son Gabriël rebuilt it and christened the country retreat ’Rust en Vruegde’ (’Rest and Joy’) — a name that symbolised country life. In 1848 Eduard van der Oudermeulen had a new neoclassical mansion with coach house built, with winding paths in park woodland of early landscape style. From 1904 it belonged to the Rotterdam shipowner Philippus van Ommeren and his wife Alida de Voogt, known for their charity. During the war the estate served as a storage and launch site for V-2 rockets and was bombed. The old mansion was demolished in 1987, but since 1961 the park has been part of the publicly accessible Wassenaarse Landgoederenzone.

nl.description: De Koninklijke Landgoederen De Horsten tussen Wassenaar en Voorschoten bestaan uit drie horsten — verhoogde strandwallen — die hun naam aan het landgoed geven: Raaphorst, Ter Horst en Eikenhorst. Prins Frederik der Nederlanden (1797–1881), de tweede zoon van koning Willem I, kocht Raaphorst en Ter Horst in 1838 en voegde er in 1846 Eikenhorst aan toe; hij woonde in het tegenovergelegen Huize De Paauw, sinds 1925 het raadhuis van Wassenaar. In 1903 kocht koningin Wilhelmina de landgoederen, die ze graag schilderend bezocht. Na haar volgden Juliana en Beatrix; in 2017 droeg Beatrix het bezit over aan koning Willem-Alexander, die met zijn gezin in villa Eikenhorst woont. De kastelen Raephorst en Ter Horst zijn verdwenen; het voormalige jachthuis van prins Frederik is nu theepaviljoen. De Seringenberg, een ruim twintig meter hoge kunstmatige heuvel, biedt uitzicht over het park.

tags: Royal estates · three horsten with park woodland and avenues
en.location: 📍 Wassenaar/Voorschoten, Wassenaar municipality · Royal estates · Large
en.description: The Royal Estates De Horsten between Wassenaar and Voorschoten consist of three horsten — raised beach ridges — which give the estate its name: Raaphorst, Ter Horst and Eikenhorst. Prince Frederik of the Netherlands (1797–1881), the second son of King Willem I, bought Raaphorst and Ter Horst in 1838 and added Eikenhorst in 1846; he lived in the opposite Huize De Paauw, the town hall of Wassenaar since 1925. In 1903 Queen Wilhelmina bought the estates, which she loved to visit and paint. After her came Juliana and Beatrix; in 2017 Beatrix transferred the property to King Willem-Alexander, who lives in villa Eikenhorst with his family. The castles Raephorst and Ter Horst have disappeared; Prince Frederik’s former hunting lodge is now a tea pavilion. The Seringenberg, an artificial hill of over twenty metres, looks out over the park.

nl.description: De Duivenvoordse en Veenzijdse Polder ligt ingeklemd tussen Den Haag, Wassenaar, Leidschendam en Voorschoten, tussen de eeuwenoude strandwallen. Het uitgestrekte, open weidegebied werd al in de middeleeuwen ontgonnen en bestaat uit hakhoutbossen, brede en smalle watergangen en weilanden vol weide-, water- en bosvogels. Het waterschap ontstond in 1877 door samenvoeging van de Duivenvoordsche (1626), Veenzijdsche (1651), Fluit- en Raaphorster polders; in 1878 verrees het eerste stoomgemaal ’De Vereeniging’ (architect J. tags: Peat meadow polder · medieval farmland between the beach ridges
en.location: 📍 Voorschoten/Leidschendam, between The Hague and Leiden · Peat meadow polder · c. 875 ha
en.description: The Duivenvoordse en Veenzijdse Polder lies wedged between The Hague, Wassenaar, Leidschendam and Voorschoten, between the age-old beach ridges. The extensive, open meadow area was reclaimed as early as the Middle Ages and consists of coppice woods, wide and narrow watercourses and meadows full of meadow, water and woodland birds. The water board was formed in 1877 by merging the Duivenvoordsche (1626), Veenzijdsche (1651), Fluit and Raaphorster polders; in 1878 the first steam pumping station ’De Vereeniging’ (architect J. Goldberg) was built, now on the municipal monument list. Staatsbosbeheer manages most of it as a protected area, where roe deer are regularly seen.

nl.location: 📍 Voorschoten, gemeente Voorschoten · Verdwenen buitenplaats · Park
nl.description: Rosenburgh in Voorschoten kent een dramatische geschiedenis. Het kasteel Rosenburg werd tussen 1281 en 1284 gebouwd door Jacob van Wassenaar, werd in 1351 verwoest tijdens de Hoekse en Kabeljauwse twisten en opnieuw tijdens het beleg van Leiden (1573–1574). In 1617 herbouwd, kwam het in 1707 in handen van luitenant-admiraal Jan Gerrit baron van Wassenaer, die er tussen 1721 en 1723 een nieuw buitenhuis liet bouwen naar ontwerp van Daniel Marot. Toen zijn enige zoon Jacob Jan in 1728 op dertienjarige leeftijd stierf, werd het voltooide lustoord in 1730 op last van de heer van Duivenvoorde geheel gesloopt — de stenen verkocht, de tuinen uitgeroeid. Sinds 1963 ligt op het terrein de gemeentelijke begraafplaats Rosenburgh; van de buitenplaats resten alleen de grachten. De oude hekpijlers staan nu bij de ingang van kasteel Duivenvoorde.

tags: Vanished country seat · now a cemetery with moats
en.location: 📍 Voorschoten, Voorschoten municipality · Vanished country seat · Park
en.description: Rosenburgh in Voorschoten has a dramatic history. The castle Rosenburg was built between 1281 and 1284 by Jacob van Wassenaar, was destroyed in 1351 during the Hook and Cod Wars and again during the siege of Leiden (1573–1574). Rebuilt in 1617, it came in 1707 into the hands of lieutenant-admiral Jan Gerrit baron van Wassenaer, who between 1721 and 1723 had a new country house built to a design by Daniel Marot. When his only son Jacob Jan died in 1728 at the age of thirteen, the completed pleasure garden was in 1730 completely demolished on the orders of the lord of Duivenvoorde — the stones sold, the gardens destroyed. Since 1963 the municipal Rosenburgh cemetery lies on the grounds; only the moats remain of the country seat. The old gate pillars now stand at the entrance to Duivenvoorde castle.

nl.description: De Leidschendammerhout bij Leidschendam is een jong, gevarieerd natuur- en recreatiegebied dat in de jaren tachtig werd aangelegd. Nog maar dertig jaar geleden liepen er zwartbonte melkkoeien op de strakke weilanden; nu ligt er een langgerekt gebied met natte bossen, ruige graslanden, riet en plassen. Schotse hooglanders grazen rond de plassen, vogels broeden in de bomen en in de winter hebben ganzen en krakeenden het riet en water overgenomen. Het gebied is te verkennen te paard, te voet of per fiets; vooral in de winter kunnen de paden flink nat zijn. In de hoek ligt vogelplas Starrevaart, tussen 1987 en 1996 gegraven als natuurcompensatie voor de zandwinning van de A4.

en.location: 📍 Leidschendam/Voorschoten, Leidschendam-Voorburg municipality · Nature and recreation area · Elongated
en.description: The Leidschendammerhout near Leidschendam is a young, varied nature and recreation area laid out in the 1980s. Barely thirty years ago black-and-white dairy cows grazed the straight meadows; now there is an elongated area of wet woodland, rough grassland, reed and lakes. Highland cattle graze around the lakes, birds breed in the trees and in winter geese and gadwalls have taken over the reed and water. The area can be explored on horseback, on foot or by bike; in winter the paths can be very wet. In one corner lies bird lake Starrevaart, dug between 1987 and 1996 as nature compensation for the sand extraction of the A4 motorway.

nl.description: Het gehucht Westeinde ligt in de Groote Westeindsche Polder (ook Westeinder Polder), een veenweidepolder die deels onder Zoeterwoude en deels onder Stompwijk valt. De polder werd in 1641 gesticht als samenvoeging van negen kleine polders; in 1852 splitste de Kleine Westeindsche Veen- en Droogmakerij zich af. Stompwijk zelf ontstond rond 1300 (als Stompic) bij de ontginning van het wilde Hollandse veen vanaf de Vliet; de boerderijen liggen merendeels aan de noordzijde en zijn via ophaalbruggen bereikbaar. In de omgeving bemaalt een molengang van drie poldermolens (Boven-, Middel- en Ondermolen uit 1672) de Driemanspolder. Het is een open, weids veenweidelandschap met sloten, kades en weidevogels.

en.location: 📍 Stompwijk, Leidschendam-Voorburg municipality · Peat meadow polder · Hamlet
en.description: The hamlet Westeinde lies in the Groote Westeindsche Polder (also Westeinder Polder), a peat meadow polder that falls partly under Zoeterwoude and partly under Stompwijk. The polder was founded in 1641 as a merger of nine small polders; in 1852 the Kleine Westeindsche Veen- en Droogmakerij split off. Stompwijk itself arose around 1300 (as Stompic) with the reclamation of the wild Dutch peat from the Vliet; the farmhouses lie mostly on the north side and are reached by drawbridges. Nearby, a chain of three polder mills (Boven-, Middel- and Ondermolen of 1672) drains the Driemanspolder. It is an open, expansive peat meadow landscape with ditches, banks and meadow birds.

nl.description: De Wilck, halverwege Zoetermeer en Alphen aan den Rijn, is een weidevogelreservaat van ruim 120 hectare vochtig en nat grasland — een prachtig voorbeeld van het ouderwetse Hollands-Utrechtse veenweidegebied. Het dankt zijn naam aan het veenstroompje De Wilck, waarvan de Slingerwetering een deel van de oude loop volgt. Het reservaat (Staatsbosbeheer) is sinds 30 maart 2000 Europees Vogelrichtlijngebied voor de kleine zwaan, die hier in de winter met meer dan één procent van de populatie verbleef. In het voorjaar broeden er grutto’s (ongeveer zeventig paren, stabiel), tureluurs, scholeksters en kieviten, en eenden als slobeend en zomertaling. De hogesnelheidslijn duikt via een geboorde tunnel op dertig meter diepte onder het reservaat door.

tags: Meadow bird reserve · wet grassland with winter guests
en.location: 📍 Hazerswoude-Rijndijk, Alphen aan den Rijn municipality · Meadow bird reserve · c. 120 ha
en.description: De Wilck, halfway between Zoetermeer and Alphen aan den Rijn, is a meadow bird reserve of over 120 hectares of damp and wet grassland — a fine example of the old-fashioned Dutch-Utrecht peat meadow country. It owes its name to the peat stream De Wilck, part of whose old course the Slingerwetering follows. Since 30 March 2000 the reserve (Staatsbosbeheer) has been a European Birds Directive site for the Bewick’s swan, which wintered here with more than one per cent of the population. In spring godwits (about seventy pairs, stable), redshanks, oystercatchers and lapwings breed, together with ducks such as shoveler and garganey. The high-speed railway line runs in a bored tunnel at thirty metres depth beneath the reserve.

nl.location: 📍 Hazerswoude-Rijndijk/Koudekerk, gemeente Alphen aan den Rijn · Rivierdijk · Lang lint
nl.description: De Rijndijk is de eeuwenoude dijk langs de Oude Rijn, tussen Leiden en Alphen aan den Rijn, met het langgerekte dorp Hazerswoude-Rijndijk dat er zijn naam aan dankt. Langs de rivier loopt het jaagpad, waar vroeger paarden de trekschuiten tussen Leiden en Utrecht voorttrokken; de paarden werden regelmatig ’ververst’ en overgezet bij de Boerenschouw en de Prinsenschouw. Aan de dijk liggen oude boerderijen in karakteristieke lintbebouwing, en molens als de Rijnenburgermolen (1722), die de Rijnenburgerpolder tot 1965 bemaalde. Bij Koudekerk stond tot 1838 het overzetveer ’de Olde Schouw’, dat werd vervangen door een stenen boogbrug; de huidige Koudekerkse brug dateert van 1929. Vanaf de dijk kijk je uit over de weidse polders van het Groene Hart.

en.location: 📍 Hazerswoude-Rijndijk/Koudekerk, Alphen aan den Rijn municipality · River dike · Long ribbon
en.description: The Rijndijk is the age-old dike along the Oude Rijn, between Leiden and Alphen aan den Rijn, with the elongated village of Hazerswoude-Rijndijk that takes its name from it. Along the river runs the towpath, where horses once pulled the trekschuiten (passenger barges) between Leiden and Utrecht; the horses were regularly ’refreshed’ and ferried across at the Boerenschouw and the Prinsenschouw. Along the dike lie old farmhouses in characteristic ribbon development, and mills such as the Rijnenburgermolen (1722), which drained the Rijnenburgerpolder until 1965. At Koudekerk stood the ferry ’de Olde Schouw’ until 1838, replaced by a stone arch bridge; the present Koudekerkse brug dates from 1929. From the dike you look out over the wide polders of the Groene Hart.

en.location: 📍 Hazerswoude-Rijndijk, Alphen aan den Rijn municipality · Polder bank · c. 1.3 km
en.description: The Kruiskade lies on the north side of the former Rietveldse polder, in the area nowadays called the Spookverlaat. The bank was laid out in 1470 for the reclamation of the Hoornse polder on the Rijn; after 1648 it formed the water divide between the Hoornse and the Rietveldse polders, each with its own water level and mills. In 1659 a verlaat (small lock) was built in the Dwarswetering, which in the nineteenth century came to be called ’spookverlaat’ (’ghost lock’) after a legend; it was demolished in 1960. After a land consolidation the surroundings were given a green purpose with tree planting and ponds. The more than 1300-metre-long bank lies between the Compierekade and the Papenvaart.

en.location: 📍 Hazerswoude-Dorp/Alphen aan den Rijn · Polder banks · c. 7 ha
en.description: The Spijkerboorsekade and the Coppierenkade lie south of Alphen aan den Rijn, on the border of the peat meadow country and the Boskoop nurseries. The Spijkerboorse Kade (7 hectares, Zuid-Hollands Landschap) was traditionally a bank with a wood bank, probably laid out to shelter the vulnerable nurseries from the wind. Along the narrow unpaved path stand pollards, a historic coppice of black alder and ash, and a pool full of amphibians and dragonflies. In the clean ditch water grows water soldier (krabbenscheer), a demanding floating plant, and along the banks flower ragged robin and water mint with its fresh peppermint scent. Near the Coppierenkade stood the Rietveldse (Behoude Kost) mill already before 1615.

en.description: The Noorderhout lies on the northern edge of Gouda, near the Plaswijck district, and forms a green noise barrier along the A12. The wall was built from large quantities of rubble; this rubble dump was covered in the 1970s with a thick layer of earth and planted. Since then it has grown into a surprisingly rich nature area with a varied flora and fauna, where rabbits are plentiful and in May the flowers bloom profusely. There is a nature playground and a dense network of footpaths; in wet weather it can be soggy. The KNNV organises plant excursions there (among others for marsh woundwort), and it lies close to the Reeuwijkse Plassen and the Goudse Hout.

nl.description: De Reeuwijkse Plassen tussen Bodegraven en Gouda vormen een mozaïek van dertien plassen met een totale oppervlakte van zo’n 735 hectare, ontstaan door turfwinning in de zeventiende en achttiende eeuw. Smalle legakkers en kades, beplant met elzen, wilgen, populieren, essen en berken, scheiden de plassen van elkaar — een typisch Hollands plassenlandschap. Aan het eind van de negentiende eeuw waren er plannen om de plassen droog te leggen, maar die werden dankzij de Goudse en Reeuwijkse natuurbescherming en watersporters terzijde geschoven. In de zomer broeden er zwarte sterns en rietzangers, in de winter strijken smienten en grote zilverreigers neer. Bijzonder zijn de kievietsbloem en de ringslang, die hier in opmars is.

tags: Lake district · thirteen turf lakes between Gouda and Bodegraven
en.location: 📍 Reeuwijk, Bodegraven-Reeuwijk municipality · Lake district · c. 735 ha
en.description: The Reeuwijkse Plassen between Bodegraven and Gouda form a mosaic of thirteen lakes with a total area of about 735 hectares, created by turf extraction in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Narrow legakkers (strips of land) and banks, planted with alders, willows, poplars, ashes and birches, separate the lakes — a typical Dutch lake landscape. At the end of the nineteenth century there were plans to reclaim the lakes, but these were set aside thanks to the nature conservationists and water-sports enthusiasts of Gouda and Reeuwijk. In summer black terns and reed warblers breed here; in winter wigeons and great egrets settle. Special are the snake’s head fritillary and the grass snake, which is on the rise here.

en.description: Het Steinse Groen lies on the east side of Gouda, wedged between the Gouda–Woerden railway and the Steinsedijk, close to the Goverwelle district. The elongated site — about 200 metres wide and 1250 metres long — is an important link between the Reeuwijkse Plassen and the Krimpenerwaard. Besides its recreational function, new nature has been laid out with herb-rich grassland, wet hay meadow, reed marsh and peat marsh, providing habitat for species such as the otter, water shrew, grass snake, green hawker and natterjack toad. Three kingfisher walls have been placed, together with a nature playground and, towards the Hollandsche IJssel, the floodplain with a pool. The last part is being laid out as new nature on the Hofstede Kloosterstein farm.

De Benschopperwetering — een zestien kilometer lange, kaarsrechte wetering vanaf IJsselstein — vormde de ontginningsas, waarlangs kolonisten lange stroken land (’cope’) kregen tegen afdracht van een tiende van de opbrengst aan de ’copers’. Nog altijd is dit copelandschap na bijna duizend jaar tot in detail beleefbaar. De boerderijen staan in een lang lint aan de ontginningsas; boerderij Rosenboom (Benedeneind, 1561) is een van de oudste van de Lopikerwaard. Houtkades met wilgen en eiken leverden het geriefhout. Het westen van de Lopikerwaard maakte deel uit van de Oude Hollandse Waterlinie.

tags: Peat meadow polder · cope reclamation in the Lopikerwaard
en.location: 📍 Benschop, Lopik municipality · Peat meadow polder · Cope landscape
en.description: Benschop lies in the heart of the Lopikerwaard, a peat meadow area reclaimed around 1100 on the orders of the bishop of Utrecht. The Benschopperwetering — a sixteen-kilometre-long, dead-straight waterway from IJsselstein — formed the reclamation axis, along which colonists received long strips of land (’cope’) in return for a tenth of the yield to the ’copers’. Even today, after nearly a thousand years, this cope landscape can be read in every detail. The farmhouses stand in a long ribbon along the reclamation axis; the Rosenboom farm (Benedeneind, 1561) is one of the oldest in the Lopikerwaard. Wood banks of willow and oak provided the geriefhout (farm timber). The west of the Lopikerwaard was part of the Oude Hollandse Waterlinie.

nl.location: 📍 Soest, gemeente Soest · Bos, heide en stuifduinen · Groot
nl.description: De bos- en natuurterreinen van Soest op de Utrechtse Heuvelrug draaien om de Soesterduinen: de Lange en Korte Duinen, het grootste stuifzandgebied van de Heuvelrug en een van de laatste plekken in Nederland met levend stuifzand. Het zand kwam op drift door eeuwen van kappen, branden, overbegrazing en plaggen — een van de eerste Nederlandse ’milieurampen’. Rondom liggen landgoed De Paltz, de hoge Stompert met zijn strubbenbossen, de voormalige Vliegbasis Soesterberg (nu park met het Nationaal Militair Museum) en de bossen van Hooge en Lage Vuursche. Onder het programma ’Laat maar Waaien’ houdt begrazing en plaggen het stuifzand in leven. Soest zelf is een lintdorp op de grens van de eng en de Eempolder.

tags: Woodland and drift sand · the Soesterduinen and surrounding grounds
en.location: 📍 Soest, Soest municipality · Woodland, heath and drift sand · Large
en.description: The woods and nature grounds of Soest on the Utrechtse Heuvelrug revolve around the Soesterduinen: the Lange and Korte Duinen, the largest drift-sand area of the Heuvelrug and one of the last places in the Netherlands with living drift sand. The sand was set adrift by centuries of felling, burning, overgrazing and turf cutting — one of the first Dutch ’environmental disasters’. Around it lie the De Paltz estate, the high Stompert with its coppice woods, the former Soesterberg Air Base (now a park with the National Military Museum) and the woods of Hooge and Lage Vuursche. Under the ’Laat maar Waaien’ (’Let it Blow’) programme, grazing and turf cutting keep the drift sand alive. Soest itself is a ribbon village on the border of the eng and the Eempolder.

nl.description: De Birkt is een historisch buurtschap tussen Amersfoort en Soest, dat zich uitstrekte tussen de Eem in het noorden en de heide en stuifduinen in het zuiden. De naam verwijst naar de vroegere berkenbossen (’birk’). Het lint bestond uit twee nederzettingen: De Lage Birkt aan de oude Ne(d)erweg (sinds 1935 de Peter van den Breemerweg) en De Hoge Birkt langs de Soesterstraatweg. Aan de Birkstraat lagen begin zeventiende eeuw vijftien boerderijen, elk met een eigen strook grond van de Eem tot aan de Soesterduinen. Omdat hun akkers pal tegen het oprukkende stuifzand lagen, legden de boeren barrièreduinen aan — houtwallen met eiken — om het land te beschermen. Vlakbij liggen het Monnikenbos en Birkhoven, genoemd naar het klooster Mariënhove (1419).

tags: Hamlet · historic ribbon between the Eem and the Soesterduinen
en.location: 📍 Soest/Amersfoort, Soest municipality · Hamlet · Historic ribbon
en.description: De Birkt is a historic hamlet between Amersfoort and Soest, stretching between the Eem in the north and the heath and drift sands in the south. The name refers to the former birch woods (’birk’). The ribbon consisted of two settlements: De Lage Birkt on the old Ne(d)erweg (since 1935 the Peter van den Breemerweg) and De Hoge Birkt along the Soesterstraatweg. Along the Birkstraat stood fifteen farms in the early seventeenth century, each with its own strip of land from the Eem to the Soesterduinen. Because their fields lay directly against the advancing drift sand, the farmers built barrier dunes — wood banks with oaks — to protect the land. Close by lie the Monnikenbos and Birkhoven, named after the Mariënhove monastery (1419).

nl.location: 📍 Amersfoort, gemeente Amersfoort · Landgoedbos · ca. 60 ha
nl.description: Birkhoven en Bokkeduinen is een parkachtig bos en voormalig landgoed ten westen van Amersfoort, op de rand van de Utrechtse Heuvelrug. In de middeleeuwen behoorde het land tot het klooster Mariënhof, waaraan het nabijgelegen Monnikenbos nog herinnert. Eind achttiende eeuw was het bezit van de burgemeestersfamilie Methorst; in 1824 vestigde Jan Cock Blomhoff zich er — het laatste opperhoofd van de Nederlandse factorij op het Japanse Decima — en liet er een landhuis bouwen. Het goed kreeg in de volksmond de naam ’Japanse bosjes’. In 1907 werd de gemeente Amersfoort eigenaar: het huis werd hotel-restaurant en dwars door het bos kwam de Barchman Wuytierslaan, waarvan het oostelijk deel Bokkeduinen ging heten. In de jaren dertig volgden de bosvijver, uitzichtheuvel, pinetum en het Bosbad; sinds 1948 ligt Dierenpark Amersfoort in de zuidoosthoek. De rododendronvallei en beukenlanen herinneren aan de Engelse landschapsstijl.

tags: Estate woodland · park wood with rhododendron valley and pinetum
en.location: 📍 Amersfoort, Amersfoort municipality · Estate woodland · c. 60 ha
en.description: Birkhoven en Bokkeduinen is a park-like wood and former estate west of Amersfoort, on the edge of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. In the Middle Ages the land belonged to the Mariënhof monastery, still recalled by the nearby Monnikenbos. In the late eighteenth century it belonged to the mayoral Methorst family; in 1824 Jan Cock Blomhoff settled here — the last opperhoofd of the Dutch trading post on Decima, Japan — and had a mansion built. The estate was popularly known as the ’Japanese copses’. In 1907 the municipality of Amersfoort became owner: the house became a hotel-restaurant and the Barchman Wuytierslaan was cut through the wood, the eastern part of which came to be called Bokkeduinen. In the 1930s followed the woodland pond, viewpoint hill, pinetum and the Bosbad (outdoor pool); since 1948 Dierenpark Amersfoort lies in the south-east corner. The rhododendron valley and beech avenues recall the English landscape style.

en.description: The De Paltz estate lies between Soest and Soesterberg, on the southern flank of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. The estate is named after a group of German refugees from the Rheinland-Pfalz, the Palatinate, who found a safe haven here in the mid-eighteenth century. The property had many owners, each leaving their mark on the beech avenues, stately buildings and the rolling valley. Since 1993 it has been owned by the singer and theatre-maker Herman van Veen, who founded the Herman van Veen Arts Center here; exhibitions, lectures and performances are held in the wooded surroundings. A marked route of just over three kilometres leads past the white mansion, the valley and through the mixed woodland, where sculptures appear along the paths.

tags: Vliegbasispark · heide en militair erfgoed op de voormalige vliegbasis
nl.location: 📍 Soesterberg, gemeente Soest · Natuur- en erfgoedpark · Groot
nl.description: Park Vliegbasis Soesterberg is de bakermat van de Nederlandse militaire luchtvaart. Op het heideveld bij Soesterberg werd in 1913 de Luchtvaartafdeling van de Koninklijke Landmacht opgericht; decennialang was de basis hermetisch afgesloten. In de Tweede Wereldoorlog namen de Duitsers het terrein als Fliegerhorst in gebruik, waarna het eind van de oorlog grotendeels werd vernietigd. Tijdens de Koude Oorlog werd het een NAVO-basis met Camp New Amsterdam en het Amerikaanse 32nd Tactical Fighter Squadron; pas in 1994 vertrokken de Amerikanen. In 2008 sloot de basis definitief en werd het terrein overgedragen aan de provincie Utrecht. Sinds 2014 is het een park met heide, bos en stilte, waar de langste militaire landingsbaan (3077 m) en het munitiepark met bunkers uit de Koude Oorlog bewaard bleven. In Hangaar 8 (1928) staat de oudste hangar van Nederland; het Nationaal Militair Museum vertelt het verhaal.

tags: Air base park · heath and military heritage on the former air base
en.location: 📍 Soesterberg, Soest municipality · Nature and heritage park · Large
en.description: Park Vliegbasis Soesterberg is the cradle of Dutch military aviation. On the heathland at Soesterberg the Aviation Department of the Royal Army was founded in 1913; for decades the base was hermetically sealed off. In the Second World War the Germans took the terrain as a Fliegerhorst, after which it was largely destroyed at the end of the war. During the Cold War it became a NATO base with Camp New Amsterdam and the American 32nd Tactical Fighter Squadron; the Americans left only in 1994. In 2008 the base closed for good and the terrain was transferred to the province of Utrecht. Since 2014 it has been a park of heath, woodland and silence, where the longest military runway (3077 m) and the ammunition park with Cold War bunkers survive. Hangaar 8 (1928) is the oldest hangar in the Netherlands; the National Military Museum tells the story.

nl.description: De Vlasakkers is een militair oefenterrein en natuurgebied van zo’n 260 hectare ten westen van Amersfoort, op een van oost naar west lopende heuvelkam van de Utrechtse Heuvelrug. Het reliëfrijke terrein — hoogste punt 54 meter — werd in de ijstijden opgestuwd en draagt prehistorische grafheuvels. De naam herinnert aan de vroegere vlasteelt, grondstof voor touw en lijnzaadolie. Sinds 1872 traint het leger er, naast de Bernhardkazerne; de decennia van rust maakten het tot een zeldzaam rijk natuurgebied met eeuwenoud eikenhakhout (elke tien tot vijftien jaar gekapt), droge heide, zandverstuivingen en oude beuken en grove dennen. Het terrein is doorgaans gesloten, maar enkele keren per jaar open tijdens georganiseerde wandel- en fietstochten.

en.location: 📍 Amersfoort/Soest, Amersfoort municipality · Military training area · c. 260 ha
en.description: De Vlasakkers is a military training area and nature reserve of some 260 hectares west of Amersfoort, on an east-west ridge of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. The relief-rich terrain — highest point 54 metres — was pushed up during the ice ages and carries prehistoric burial mounds. The name recalls the former flax cultivation, the raw material for rope and linseed oil. Since 1872 the army has trained here, next to the Bernhardkazerne; the decades of quiet made it a remarkably rich nature area with centuries-old oak coppice (cut every ten to fifteen years), dry heath, drift-sand patches and old beeches and Scots pines. The terrain is usually closed, but opens a few times a year for organised walking and cycling tours.

nl.location: 📍 Soesterberg/Zeist, gemeente Soest · Voormalig militair kamp · Heide en bos
nl.description: Het Oude Kamp bij Soesterberg herinnert aan twee eeuwen militaire geschiedenis op de heide. In 1818 liet koning Willem I er een groot zomerkamp inrichten naar voorbeeld van het Franse Camp d’Utrecht: een vier kilometer lang terrein van de Oude Postweg tot Kampoord, met 24 waterputten — één per bataljon. De soldaten bivakkeerden er in tenten. Het verste deel van het kampterrein staat sindsdien bekend als het Oude Kamp; de genie (mineurs en sappeurs) oefende er met loopgraven en veldversterkingen, die nog altijd in het landschap te zien zijn. Tijdens de Eerste Wereldoorlog werd het uitgebreide kamp interneringskamp voor 12.000 Belgische militairen. Het terrein bleef eeuwenlang militair, maar het meest westelijke deel is inmiddels teruggegeven aan de natuur, waar heide, bos en zandvlaktes weer ruimte krijgen.

tags: Former military camp · heath and woodland returning to nature
en.location: 📍 Soesterberg/Zeist, Soest municipality · Former military camp · Heath and woodland
en.description: The Oude Kamp near Soesterberg recalls two centuries of military history on the heath. In 1818 King Willem I had a large summer camp laid out here on the model of the French Camp d’Utrecht: a four-kilometre terrain from the Oude Postweg to Kampoord, with 24 wells — one per battalion. The soldiers bivouacked in tents. The furthest part of the camp has since been known as the Oude Kamp; the engineers (sappers and miners) practised there with trenches and field fortifications, still visible in the landscape today. During the First World War the enlarged camp became an internment camp for 12,000 Belgian soldiers. The terrain remained military for centuries, but the westernmost part has now been returned to nature, where heath, woodland and sand flats are regaining space.

en.description: Klein Zwitserland (’Little Switzerland’) is a hilly woodland of some 36 hectares on the south-west flank of the Amersfoortse Berg, an offshoot of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. The name refers to the rolling relief. The wood originated as an oak-bark forest — the bark supplied tannin for the tanneries — and later provided sand and gravel for building; only from 1930 was it laid out as a walking area. A 3.5-kilometre route leads past historical highlights, including a burial mound and the Belgenmonument, which commemorates the Belgian refugees of the First World War. The wood borders the Stichtse Rotonde and is a beloved urban wood for short, varied walks.

en.description: The Nimmerdor estate on the southern edge of Amersfoort goes back to 1660, when esquire Everard Meyster bought nine hectares on the Leusderheide and had a mansion built. The name means ’never dry’: Meyster had planting laid out so it would never look dry and bare. The estate grew to about 100 hectares, of which 48 remain today, with a mixed woodland of conifers and broadleaves and a toad pond. Unique are the avenue structures with seventeenth-century sightlines and the star wood of the eighteenth century. The western part is a public walking wood; the part around the mansion is still private. A circular walk of about five kilometres starts on the Leusderweg, just after the viaduct under the A28.

en.description: The Lockhorsterbos lies on the dividing line between the Utrechtse Heuvelrug and the Eemvallei, on the edge of Leusden and Amersfoort, and is bounded on the east by the Heiligenbergerbeek, whose water is fed by clean seepage from the Heuvelrug. The small wood (7.5 hectares) was in 1927 the very first purchase of Stichting Het Utrechts Landschap. It owes its name to the patrician Lockhorst family, whose knightly manor is already mentioned in 1254. In the wood, young trees alternate with stately oaks and beeches of more than two hundred years old. It is a refuge for almost all native tits and woodpeckers, the bullfinch, the robin and occasionally the kingfisher.

en.description: The Bossen achter Rusthof lie around the Rusthof general cemetery near Leusden and largely belong to the Den Treek-Henschoten estate, the largest family estate in the Netherlands. It is a relief-rich walking area full of geological features: drift-sand cliffs, the bank-shaped Ringheuvels, blow-out hollows and still-active drift sands. The valley-like depression of the Hazenwater, the Langeveen and the Waswater bear witness to a drift-sand landscape that once prevailed here; the former Vogelwater was reclaimed in the nineteenth century and is now called the Droogmakerij. Geopad 108 leads in routes of 3.8 and 5 kilometres through the area, where the Rusthof cemetery has been extended into the woods.

en.location: 📍 Lunteren, Ede municipality · Sand-extraction lake · c. 9.5 ha
en.description: The Grote Veenderplas — also called the Mobagat — lies in the Gelderse Vallei near Lunteren, along the A30, the Scherpenzeelseweg and the Renswoudsestraatweg. The lake arose in the early 1970s through sand extraction for the A30 motorway and is an old-fashioned, deep sand pit of about 9.5 hectares, 15 to 17 metres at its deepest. The water consists of seepage water from the Veluwe and is therefore clear. Around it lies a green mantle of trees and shrubs, making the lake an oasis of calm. The fishing water is leased by Hengelsportvereniging Barneveld; it holds carp, tench, ide, pike and perch. The SBNL Natuurfonds manages the lake, where nature-friendly banks and a toad pond have been created after the redevelopment.

en.location: 📍 Bosch en Duin, Zeist municipality · Drift-sand woodland · Former drift sand
en.description: The Panbos near Bosch en Duin is a former drift-sand landscape, directly bordering the Beerschoten estate. Only a few small patches of the old sand flats remain, but most of the area is now covered in conifer forest. Characteristic are the old Scots pines on the edge of the sand flats, whose root systems have been exposed by the wind; in one such pine a group of long-eared owls roosts in winter. On the dry, warm sand grow dozens of juniper shrubs, typical pioneers of drift sand, and the sand lizard and many insects live here. The Tannenberg is a hill in the wood covered with distinctive pines. Het Utrechts Landschap manages this varied sports and walking area.

The village is still characterised by broad avenues, old trees and much greenery, surrounded by the Panbos, the Beerschoten estate and the woods of Zeist.

Dijnselburg gaat terug tot de middeleeuwse hof Dinslo; in 1845 was het een boerenhofstede die de familie Nepveu — van Franse komaf — tot lustplaats maakte. Laurent Théodore Nepveu stichtte er in 1812 een particuliere begraafplaats; het huidige landhuis in neorenaissancestijl met speklagen dateert van 1883, met ernaast het markante Philosophicum. In de jaren zestig verrees op de grond van Vollenhove het gelijknamige hoogbouwplan met 2.250 woningen; het park van Dijnselburg bleef als gemeentelijk monument bewaard.

en.description: Dijnselburg and Vollenhove are two country seats on the edge of Zeist with an eventful history. Dijnselburg goes back to the medieval manor Dinslo; in 1845 it was a farmstead which the Nepveu family — of French origin — turned into a pleasure seat. Laurent Théodore Nepveu founded a private cemetery there in 1812; the present mansion in neo-Renaissance style with speckled brickwork dates from 1883, with the striking Philosophicum beside it. Vollenhove was originally a farm of the Oostbroek monastery and became a country seat around 1800, bought in 1827 by governor-general Godert van der Capellen. In the 1960s the high-rise plan Vollenhove with 2,250 homes rose on its grounds; the Dijnselburg park survives as a municipal monument.

en.description: The Sandwyck estate in De Bilt was originally a grange of the Oostbroek monastery. In 1964 the estate came into the hands of Utrecht University and fell into disrepair, until Het Utrechts Landschap took it over in 1989 and restored it. The Van Boetzelaerpark was donated to the municipality. The estate is about 45 hectares and freely accessible.

nl.description: Fort bij Rijnaauwen is het grootste fort van de Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie. Het werd tussen 1868 en 1871 gebouwd bij Bunnik en verdedigde samen met Fort bij Vechten de Houtense Vlakte en de Kromme Rijn. Het fort is nooit in gevechten betrokken geweest en groeide uit tot een natuurfort vol bijzondere planten en dieren. Bekend is het paddenstoelenparadijs: nergens in Nederland groeien zoveel soorten op een fort. Ook leven er zeven soorten vleermuizen, waaronder de rosse vleermuis, die in de bomvrije gebouwen overwinteren. Staatsbosbeheer beheert het fort, dat alleen met een gids te bezoeken is; onderweg zijn resten te zien van een oude loopgraaf en een kruitmagazijn.

en.location: 📍 Bunnik, Bunnik municipality · Fort · Guided access only
en.description: Fort bij Rijnaauwen is the largest fort of the Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie. It was built between 1868 and 1871 near Bunnik and, together with Fort bij Vechten, defended the Houtense Vlakte and the Kromme Rijn. The fort was never involved in fighting and grew into a nature fort full of special plants and animals. It is known as a mushroom paradise: nowhere in the Netherlands do so many species grow on a single fort. Seven species of bat also live here, including the common noctule, which hibernate in the bomb-proof buildings. Staatsbosbeheer manages the fort, which can only be visited with a guide; en route one sees remains of an old trench and a powder magazine.

nl.description: Fort bij Vechten is na Rijnaauwen het grootste fort van de Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie. Het werd tussen 1867 en 1870 gebouwd op een strategische plek: bij het fort takte de Oude Rijn af van de Kromme Rijn, en al in de Romeinse tijd lag hier het castellum Fectio, waarvan resten op het terrein zijn gevonden. en.location: 📍 Bunnik, Bunnik municipality · Fort · National Waterliniemuseum
en.description: Fort bij Vechten is, after Rijnaauwen, the largest fort of the Nieuwe Hollandse Waterlinie. It was built between 1867 and 1870 at a strategic spot: here the Oude Rijn branched off from the Kromme Rijn, and in Roman times the castellum Fectio already stood here, remains of which have been found on the site. The fort counts 17 hectares, sixteen bomb-proof buildings and no fewer than sixteen million bricks. It never came to a battle. In winter, five species of bat hibernate here. Since May 2015 the Waterliniemuseum has been housed on the fort, with a 50-metre-long scale model of the entire waterline.

Oud-Dennenoord was founded by banker Jan Kol, who also owned De Breul; the villa on the site of today’s Antropia burned down, was rebuilt as the Rose-Villa and was bombed in the Second World War. en.description: The Wulperhorst country seat lies on the south-east side of Zeist, between Slot Zeist and Blikkenburg, as a link in the Stichtse Lustwarande. Its history goes back to 1692, when the manor of Stoetwegen was mentioned. The eighteenth-century Huys Wulperhorst had a formal layout with a water avenue, a moat over one and a half kilometres long, a star wood and an orchard. In 1829 it passed to Jan Elias Huydecoper, who also acquired Slot Zeist and had J.D. Zocher jr. design a kilometre-long vista between the two houses. The present mansion dates from 1858, to a design by S.A. van Lunteren; the old ice cellar survives. The eye-catcher is the ’grand canal’, a watery sightline where the kingfisher hunts. On a field, Het Utrechts Landschap grows the old grain ’Utrechtse Blauwe’.

Around 1850 this was the holiday area of wealthy merchants and bankers from Amsterdam and Utrecht. Well-known names are Hoog Beek en Royen (1824, with winding ponds by Zocher), Pavia with its winding pond, Molenbosch (1837, founded by banker Stoop) and the later Nieuw Beerschoten. The parks run into each other and, with the Zeisterbos, form a continuous walking area full of rhododendrons, old avenues and mansions.

tags: Woodland · centuries-old walking wood with sprengen and estates
en.location: 📍 Zeist, Zeist municipality · Woodland · c. 200 ha walking wood
en.description: The Zeisterbos east of Zeist is, by Dutch standards, an exceptionally old wood: many trees are well over 200 years old. It originally belonged to the Beek en Royen country seat (1771), laid out in strict baroque style with the Woudenbergseweg as its sightline. From 1795 Scots pines were planted as production forest. In 1913 the municipality of Zeist bought the wood to preserve it as a walking wood; since 1994 Het Utrechts Landschap has been the owner. Characteristic are the sprengen — hand-dug spring brooks that supplied the ponds and fountains of the estates and have largely dried up through desiccation. The rich forest floor with Solomon’s seal and bilberry attracts redstart, tawny owl and goldcrest. Worth seeing are the Jagershuis, the Boskapel and the deer park.

nl.location: 📍 Zeist, gemeente Zeist · Bos · Tussen Zeist, Soesterberg en Austerlitz
nl.description: Het Zeisterwoud is de uitgestrekte bosgordel ten oosten van Zeist, die doorloopt richting Soesterberg en Austerlitz. Het is de noordelijke voortzetting van het Zeisterbos, op de zandgronden van de Utrechtse Heuvelrug, waar heide en stuifzand ooit domineerden en vanaf de achttiende eeuw grootschalig bos werd aangeplant. De oude Kampweg voert door het woud naar de vroegere vliegbasis Soesterberg en herinnert aan het Franse legerkamp uit 1804. en.location: 📍 Zeist, Zeist municipality · Woodland · Between Zeist, Soesterberg and Austerlitz
en.description: The Zeisterwoud is the extensive forest belt east of Zeist, running on towards Soesterberg and Austerlitz. It is the northern continuation of the Zeisterbos, on the sandy soils of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug, where heath and drift sand once dominated and forest was planted on a large scale from the eighteenth century. The old Kampweg leads through the wood to the former Soesterberg air base and recalls the French army camp of 1804. The mixed conifer and broadleaf woodland — Scots pine and Douglas fir beside birch, pedunculate oak and rowan — is gradually being converted to more natural forest. The wood is popular with walkers and riders and forms part of Utrechtse Heuvelrug National Park.

tags: Dorp en bos · Napoleontisch dorp met pyramide in de boswachterij
nl.location: 📍 Austerlitz, gemeente Zeist · Dorp en bos · Nationaal Park Utrechtse Heuvelrug
nl.description: Austerlitz is een klein dorp midden in de bossen van de Utrechtse Heuvelrug, dat zijn bestaan dankt aan de Franse tijd. In 1804 sloeg generaal Auguste de Marmont hier met zijn Bataafs-Franse leger het kamp op; om de manschappen bezig te houden liet hij op het hoogste punt van de Heuvelrug een aarden piramide opwerpen als eerbetoon aan Napoleon, naar het voorbeeld van Gizeh. De piramide — 36 meter hoog, met obelisk — is het best bewaarde Napoleontische monument van Nederland en geldt als historisch hoogtepunt van het Nationaal Park. Het dorp dankt zijn naam aan de Slag bij Austerlitz. Na het vertrek van de Fransen werd de heide ontgonnen en bebost; in 1939 kocht Staatsbosbeheer de landgoederen Wallenburg en Austerlitz, waaruit boswachterij Austerlitz ontstond.

tags: Village and woodland · Napoleonic village with pyramid in the forest
en.location: 📍 Austerlitz, Zeist municipality · Village and woodland · Utrechtse Heuvelrug National Park
en.description: Austerlitz is a small village amid the woods of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug that owes its existence to the French era. In 1804 general Auguste de Marmont encamped here with his Batavian-French army; to keep the men occupied he had an earthen pyramid raised on the highest point of the Heuvelrug as a tribute to Napoleon, after the example of Giza. The pyramid — 36 metres high, with obelisk — is the best-preserved Napoleonic monument in the Netherlands and a historic high point of the National Park. The village takes its name from the Battle of Austerlitz. After the French left, the heath was reclaimed and afforested; in 1939 Staatsbosbeheer bought the Wallenburg and Austerlitz estates, from which boswachterij Austerlitz arose.

De Kozakkenput dankt zijn naam aan de waterputten die de kozakken — onderdeel van de troepen van koning Willem I — hier in 1813 groeven bij hun bivak; de oorspronkelijke put is nog als diep gat herkenbaar. De Krakeling was in de Franse tijd een boerderij met bakkerij en slagerij voor het bezettingsleger; later ontstond er een zandgroeve met een poel die als enige permanent water voert. Hazelworm en boompieper voelen zich er thuis.

tags: Woodland and heath · French well and sand quarry on the old Woudenberg road
en.location: 📍 Zeist–Austerlitz, Zeist municipality · Woodland and heath · East of the Zeisterbos
en.description: East of the Zeisterbos lie the Kozakkenput and De Krakeling, a varied area of woodland, heath and fields along the medieval Woudenbergse Zandweg from Utrecht to Woudenberg. The Kozakkenput owes its name to the wells that the Cossacks — part of the troops of King William I — dug here in 1813 at their bivouac; the original well is still visible as a deep pit. The Krakeling was, in the French era, a farm with a bakery and butcher’s for the occupying army; later a sand quarry arose with a pool that is the only permanently water-bearing one. Since 1996 Het Utrechts Landschap has managed most of the Zeisterbos, the Kozakkenput and the Krakeling quarry; part of the wood has been converted back to heath. Slow worm and tree pipit feel at home here.

en.location: 📍 Leusden–Woudenberg, Leusden municipality · Estate · c. 2,200 ha
en.description: The Den Treek-Henschoten estate is the largest family estate in the Netherlands: almost 2,200 hectares of woodland, heath and farmland on the transition from the Utrechtse Heuvelrug to the Gelderse Vallei. The name Den Treek comes from the ’treck’ (trek) of the cattle to the Leusderheide; the farm is mentioned as early as 1334. In 1807 esquire W.H. de Beaufort bought the country seat and had large parts of the barren heath afforested; around 1820 the house received a park by J.D. Zocher jr. In 1919 the various family branches were merged into the present N.V. with over 500 shareholders, all descendants of De Beaufort. Highlights are the Treeker Eik (the oldest tree on the estate, germinated around 1753), the star wood, the Treekerduinen and the Koepel van Stoop. Walkers may roam freely.

en.description: Between Zeist, Driebergen and Austerlitz lie the adjoining estates of Heidestein, Bornia and Noordhout. Heidestein was the country seat of the De Wetstein Pfister family, who had a mansion built there in 1906 and enriched the grounds with a golf course, tea house, narrow-gauge railway and pond with canal; the mansion went up in flames in 1939 and the estate was donated to Het Utrechts Landschap in 1974. Noordhout is a 172-hectare estate between Austerlitz and Maarn, linked via the Mollebos ecoduct. Extensive heaths, where Drenthe heath sheep graze, show how the Heuvelrug looked a century ago.

en.location: 📍 Zeist, Zeist municipality · Estate · On the Driebergseweg
en.description: The De Breul country seat on the Driebergseweg in Zeist grew out of an old estate first mentioned in 1413 that had the status of a lordship. In 1811 the Utrecht banker Jan Kol acquired the property and around 1825–1833 had a classical house built on a raised hill, using the earth from the excavated pond. The landscape park in English style — probably by J.D. Zocher jr. — is regarded as one of the most successful of its time, with a river-like water feature and a bridge modelled on a Roman aqueduct. In 1926–28 J.W. Hanrath renovated the house. Since 1946 the Sint Willebrordusstichting with its schools has been based here; the remaining landscape park belongs to Het Utrechts Landschap. Near the Breullaan stands the gigantic Cäsar bunker with 3.5-metre-thick walls.

en.location: 📍 Driebergen-Rijsenburg, Utrechtse Heuvelrug municipality · Woodland · Between railway and built-up area
en.description: The Rijsenburgsebos lies in the woodland belt between the Utrecht–Arnhem railway and the built-up area of Driebergen-Rijsenburg. Much of it belonged to the former medieval Rijsenburg estate, with a farmstead already shown on a 1594 map and later called De Kraay. A sightline and star of paths from 1718 cut the wood like a cake into fifteen points. In the eighteenth century sprengen were dug to feed the ponds of the country seats; through desiccation they have largely dried up. After the February storm of 1953, enthusiastic municipal officials laid out the famous Heidetuin (heather garden) with hundreds of heather species on a clearing. In the Seminariebos, a Lourdes grotto recalls the former seminary.

en.description: The Driebergsebos was formerly known as the Park van Sparrendaal and still bears the features of a historic country seat: old planting, sightlines and a path structure from the era of aristocratic garden architecture. In the eighteenth century sprengenbeken were dug — shallow spring brooks with spring heads where groundwater bubbled up — which supplied the ponds of the surrounding estates with water. Through desiccation they no longer function as such, but they remain clearly visible in the landscape. The wood has a dune-like relief with valley-like hollows dug to tap groundwater. The Trage Tocht along the sprengen passes bowl-shaped ponds and the Zwitserse Brug.

De naam herinnert aan de kurkplatenfabriek die hier van 1935 tot 1970 was gevestigd; na de sloop werd het terrein aan de natuur teruggegeven. en.location: 📍 Driebergen-Rijsenburg, Utrechtse Heuvelrug municipality · Small nature area · Along the Langbroekerdijk
en.description: Along the Langbroekerdijk, just after the crossing with the Rijsenburgselaan, lies a very small nature area of Het Utrechts Landschap: De Kurk. It is one of the few areas of the foundation that are closed to the public, simply because it is too small to open. The name recalls the cork-plate factory that stood here from 1935 to 1970; after demolition the site was returned to nature. De Kurk harbours a true rarity: the snail Oestophora barbula, an Iberian endemic found only in Spain and Portugal that travelled to Driebergen as a stowaway with the cork — the only representatives in north-western Europe. A monumental willow with a girth of over five metres also stands here.

en.description: The Ludenbos in Doorn is named after the Luden family, owners of Moersbergen castle from 1897 to 1962. In 1872 mr. H.L.M. Luden bought the Der Hirtler country seat and, a few years later, thirty hectares of woodland from Moersbergen; he opened the wood as a walking wood and had the old connecting road (the Kampweg) moved northwards, creating a large continuous walking area. In 1962 Jan Anton Willem Luden bequeathed the castle with its grounds — including the Ludenbos — to Het Utrechts Landschap. The mixed woodland with open and dense parts belongs to the oldest ten per cent of the Netherlands’ forests and has an exceptionally high ecological quality.

en.description: The Huis te Maarn country seat lies on the southern part of the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. The estate covers over 200 hectares, mostly woodland with a few fine heath patches, and a landscape park. The white, neoclassical mansion — whose appearance recalls the White House in Washington — was built in 1915 to a design by architect Jan Stuyt; the founder was W.B. Blijdenstein, married to A.G. van Heek. The garden and park date from 1906 and were designed by garden architect P.H. Wattez. Characteristic are the drive from the Maarnse Grindweg with its sightline, the Lebanon cedars in the meadow and the Bentheim well. Since 1998 the house, coach house and park have been national monuments. Walking routes lead through the park woodland towards the Kaapse Bossen.

en.description: The Anderstein estate near Maarsbergen goes back to the Uilegat farmstead, which belonged to Maarsbergen castle and passed to Anna Maria de Marez after the division of 1717. Around 1852 Uilegat was demolished and replaced by a larger farm named Anderstein. In 1903 Hendrik Adriaan van Beuningen, director of the Steenkolen Handels Vereniging, bought the estate; his son Coenraad Samuel had Villa Anderstein built there in 1913/14 in English country-house style (architect Jan Stuivinga, garden by Springer) and an open-air swimming pool in 1926. Until 1985 it was a dairy farm with cheese trade; afterwards a 27-hole golf course was laid out. The Van Beuningen family still owns the estate; recently the Heijgraaf and Maarnse beek have been made water-bearing again.

en.location: 📍 Woudenberg–Scherpenzeel, Woudenberg municipality · Woodland · On the Valleikanaal
en.description: Between Woudenberg and Scherpenzeel, bordering the Valleikanaal, lies the Broekerbos, a quiet and barely accessible small woodland of Het Utrechts Landschap. It consists of much coppiced, former oak coppice on wet sandy soil; in a plot with larch a colony of grey herons has nested since about 1975. The wood forms an important resting place for roe deer and is one of four stepping stones in the ecological corridor along the Valleikanaal. In the wood, which forms part of the Grebbelinie, lies a former anti-tank ditch and in the line dike near the Broekersloot casemates can still be seen. The site is not accessible to the public; from the dike and the paths around it, it can be well experienced.

Het landgoed bestaat voor een derde uit bos en natuur — waaronder het boscomplex Berkhorst — en voor twee derde uit landbouwgrond, met monumentale schaapskooien en het oude kampenlandschap van de Vallei.

en.location: 📍 Scherpenzeel, Scherpenzeel municipality · Estate · c. 1,075 ha
en.description: The Scherpenzeel estate is, with over 1,000 hectares, one of the largest estates in the Netherlands, situated in the Gelderse Vallei. Since its first mentions in the fourteenth century it has been sold only once: in 1793 the Amsterdam merchant J.B. van Naamen, made wealthy in South Africa, bought the property, and his descendants (the Royaards family) are still the owners. The white-plastered, moated Huis Scherpenzeel received its present neo-Tudor form around 1857; it is surrounded by a landscape park with vistas. The house has belonged to the municipality since 1975 and is leased to Geldersche Kasteelen. The estate consists of one-third woodland and nature — including the Berkhorst wood complex — and two-thirds farmland, with monumental sheepfolds and the old kampen landscape of the Vallei.
